free_tier.stated: Operator-run on-demand GPU VMs with a full public rate card, no contract and no bandwidth charges. Quoted single-card rates: RTX A6000 48GB USD 0.55/hr on 6 vCPU, 32 GB RAM and 256 GB disk (alternate configuration) and USD 0.57/hr on 48 GB RAM; RTX 6000 Ada 48GB USD 0.79/hr; L40 48GB USD 0.86/hr; L40S 48GB USD 0.97/hr; A100 80GB USD 1.35/hr; A100 SXM4 80GB USD 1.38/hr; H100 80GB USD 2.73/hr on 20 vCPU, 128 GB RAM and 1250 GB disk; H100 SXM5 80GB USD 3.14/hr; H200 NVL 141GB USD 3.62/hr. Eight-card nodes: B300 SXM6 USD 52.80/hr and B200 SXM6 USD 43.46/hr.

chaining: USD 2.73 for an H100 hour with 1.25 TB of included disk is above the on-demand H100 floors found later in this same session, HyperAI PCIe at USD 1.80, Voltage Park at USD 1.99 and QuantaCloud PCIe at USD 2.59, so the reason to take this row is the bundled disk and the email-only signup rather than the rate.

page description quoted: No contracts, no bandwidth charges, and no hidden fees
the signup form asks for an email address and a password only; no card field and no company field appears on that page
the operator states it has run since 2021 and claims NVIDIA Preferred Partner status; the site names the cards it runs rather than aggregating other hosts

notes: New provider: no record in dossier/compute/. The 1250 GB of bundled disk on the H100 row is unusual at this price and is why the shape quotes that row rather than the cheapest card. Supply is asserted by a rate card with a Deploy link per row, not measured: no instance was launched. Free egress is the vendor's claim. Pre-existing A6000 rate at USD 0.55/hr sits between RunPod's USD 0.59 and TensorDock's USD 0.12 consumer floor.
